args.name: Functional food preservation
args.function: Provide a learnable, physically grounded method to slow the actual spoilage of owned known-safe food. The existing paired ground-exposure trial explicitly cannot preserve food, so an observation-only substitute does not solve this problem.
args.conditions: Moss owns three roots and five berries with known zero toxicity. These foods are ageing. Moss is outdoors on ordinary soil, has no established tools, fuel supply or storage structure, and has not established hazelnut edibility. Any prerequisites must be explicit and obtained through actual work.
args.inputs: Potentially owned roots or berries plus whatever materials a supported method genuinely requires; suitable materials and quantities are currently unknown.
args.costs: Unknown. Specify real learning time, work, material requirements, ongoing costs, interruption handling and risks before use.
args.effects: If the world supports such a method, enable a measurable reduction in subsequent food decay through actual processing or storage. Do not grant replacement food, safety certification, equipment, mastery or preservation merely for requesting it. If no functional method is supported, state that limitation plainly.

candidates.function: Place one or two whole units of an owned food on the ground as a paired exposure trial, inspect their quantity and decay, end the observation or retrieve what remains.
candidates.costs: Start: inputStackId of an owned, unspoiled, nontoxic food, quantity 1 or 2 whole units (default 2), and an unoccupied ordinary-ground x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; two work rounds at one energy each. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: target trial in reach, one round and 0.2 energy. Retrieve: operator only, one round and one energy. Cancel of an exposed trial ends observation at no cost. No supports, tools, water or fuel are used or granted.
candidates.effects: Completed setup places the samples at two ground positions 0.2 apart under the same ambient conditions; with one unit there is no matched control. No food moisture, drying or preservation model exists in this world: both samples keep the existing decay rules, so no treatment difference, preserved status, safety certification or extended lifetime is produced. The trial records rounds exposed and marks a 10-round observation checkpoint; ageing continues while unattended and after the checkpoint. Inspect records sample quantity and decay as a personal unverified record. Retrieve returns only the remaining material, never a replacement. Setup interruption keeps paid work; cancel releases reserved food once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for starting, inspecting or retrieving.

candidates.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
candidates.costs: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
candidates.effects: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

candidates.function: Plant one owned root unit in a small soil plot as a persistent trial, inspect a plot by direct observation, or take back remaining planted material; resume or cancel unfinished planting.
candidates.costs: Plant: one owned unspoiled root unit (quantity 1); two work rounds at one energy each, at an unoccupied ordinary-soil x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; supply inputStackId. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy, the baseline probe observation of a plot in reach (target). Remove: one round and 1 energy, planter only (target). Tend is unavailable and spends nothing. No tools or water are granted.
candidates.effects: Completed planting places the real root unit in the plot; it keeps ageing under existing environmental decay while the planter is absent. Plot state records stage, observation rounds, soil moisture and temperature/rain exposure. There is no propagation, growth, harvest or replenishment rule for roots, so a plot never produces food. Inspect records only visible state. Remove returns only the material that physically remains, never a replacement; the emptied plot remains. Cancel releases unplanted material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward for planting, inspecting or removing; genuine observed changes use the existing evidence-deduplicated probe feedback only.
Actual nutrition and toxicity apply. Food never directly heals. resource:ID selects an owned stack.

candidates.function: Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
candidates.costs: 2 energy per unit, finite current source stock.
candidates.effects: Transfers real source stock to inventory; requires the source interaction range. No processing or felling is implied.

candidates.function: Study an already implemented ability with its declared prerequisites.
candidates.costs: The interface-specific number of simulation rounds.
candidates.effects: Implementation does not grant mastery. Already mastered interfaces are reused without new rewards.

candidates.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
candidates.costs: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
candidates.effects: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.

candidates.function: Recover available physical energy at the current position.
candidates.effects: Base recovery 4, modified by actually accessible registered facilities; capped at 40.

response.text: {"queries":[],"result_json":"{\"reviews\":[{\"actor\":\"moss\",\"decision\":\"develop\",\"ability\":null,\"reason\":\"Develop functional air-drying in the existing current-conversation handoff. The supplied related-capability searches and registry identify no equivalent: controlled-food-processing-trial explicitly leaves decay unchanged, cultivate-plant also retains ordinary decay, and gathering or moving food does not preserve it. The current world has no implemented drying mechanism, so preservation is not presently available. That missing mechanism warrants development rather than permanent rejection or another observation-only substitute. Successful preservation must remain conditional on actual materials, food properties and drying conditions; ordinary outdoor soil alone is insufficient.\",\"specification\":\"General operation: air-dry food, parameterized by owned inputStackId, quantity, supportId/location and modes set-up, inspect, retrieve, resume and cancel. Applicable to any actor who individually learns it. Initial scope is whole food whose implemented material properties permit air-drying without cutting; no cutting tools, fire, salt, containers or storage buildings are implied. Implement this operation and its missing moisture/decay mechanism together before exposing it as usable. Do not merely rename the existing ground-exposure trial or attach a preserved label to unchanged food.\\nReferences and prerequisites: candidates include root stack item-3-moss-12, quantity 3, recorded decay 31.2865681, and berry stack item-17-moss-78, quantity 5, recorded decay 17.01287737. Revalidate ownership, remaining quantity, location, reach, spoilage and recorded food applicability at execution. The packet establishes these foods as nontoxic; drying does not establish additional safety. Hazelnut item-29-moss-139 is not an eligible known-safe food on the supplied evidence. A physically suitable, stable, uncontaminated, exposed stone support must actually exist and be accessible; bare soil is not an equivalent. start-1-stone is a remembered finite stone source, not an already owned or prepared drying surface. Reuse gather to obtain real material if needed, paying its existing 2 energy per unit and decrementing source stock; reuse navigate for actual travel at its existing costs. Source stock does not certify a gathered piece's shape or cleanliness. Validate those properties and usable area from the actual material. If no suitable support exists, setup fails without creating one; unsupported cleaning, cutting or fabrication requires its own actual mechanism, not an implied prerequisite grant.\\nCosts and work: study takes 4 simulation rounds, individually. Setup takes two active work rounds at 1 energy each for a batch of up to one food unit and reserves one real suitable stone piece with enough exposed area; larger batches require proportionate support area and two work rounds/2 energy per food unit, with fractional quantities charged proportionately and work accrued continuously. No food is consumed as a setup fee. The stone remains a recoverable physical support, not a consumed ingredient. Inspect costs one round and 0.2 energy. Retrieve costs one round and 1 energy per batch. Drying takes additional elapsed simulation time, not study or review time, and cannot promise a completion deadline before environmental conditions are known. Passive drying consumes no actor energy; heat comes from actual ambient/radiative exchange, not free heat. Food continues to age during learning, travel, setup and drying.\\nRequired minimal mechanism: add conserved water and non-water food components, exposed area, food-specific moisture transport, and a moisture-dependent spoilage rule. Initialize material components from explicit food definitions and the actual remaining food, never by restoring quantity, nutrition or freshness. Before release, define numerical moisture, transport, safe operating bounds and spoilage parameters for each supported food in executable configuration; do not silently declare roots or berries dryable without such definitions. At every simulation step compute evaporation from exposed area, food moisture, ambient temperature and air moisture; bound it by available water and the heat available for vaporization. Transfer evaporated water to the environment and debit the corresponding heat. Implement the minimum local air-moisture/heat exchange state if absent; do not assume dry weather or reveal hidden environmental values through this review. Rain or humid conditions can halt drying or cause modeled water uptake. Run spoilage using the same environmental baseline as ordinary food, multiplied by a configured, bounded moisture-dependent factor that is below 1 only when actual moisture reduction warrants it. No reduction merely for placement or active process status. Record the counterfactual baseline increment alongside the applied increment for internal verification, without presenting it as a physically observed control sample. Existing accumulated decay never decreases. Drying must not remove toxins, reverse spoilage, sterilize food, or guarantee safe storage. Reject food already ineligible for consumption rather than rehabilitating it. If the implementation cannot yet supply this mechanism, keep the feature pending development and plainly report that no functional preservation has occurred.\\nConservation and products: keep food identity and a single accountable allocation across inventory, reserved inputs and the support. Split stacks without duplicating their components or resetting age. The product is the same food with less water, changed mass and only its retained non-water nutrients; do not increase total available nutrition or convert water loss into lost edible units. Attribute any real spoilage losses to explicit waste. Integration with eat, pickup, drop and give must retain moisture, accumulated decay and ownership semantics. Returned stone is the original remaining stone, not a replacement.\\nLifecycle: setup records personal processId, reserved inputs and paid work. Interruption preserves work and reservations; uncompleted setup grants no drying benefit, and its food ages in its actual location. Resume revalidates access and remaining inputs. Cancel releases each surviving reservation exactly once, without refunding spent time or energy. Death releases reserved surviving materials at their real location and ends personal work. Once food is physically laid out, drying, wetting and spoilage continue unattended, including after cancellation of monitoring or the operator's death. Retrieval changes exposure according to the actual destination; it does not grant dry storage. Keep moisture-dependent effects on the food itself, not dependent on an active operator. No ongoing fuel or automatic maintenance is charged; turning, moving, sheltering or cleaning is not silently performed. Continued suitability depends on actual support cleanliness, exposure, weather and food condition. A damaged or contaminated support and rewetting can end the benefit. Other actors do not automatically help, maintain the batch, transfer ownership or communicate observations.\\nImplementation reuse: record exact reuse of gather, navigate, learn, eat and applicable existing item-transfer/decay code in the development change record. Reuse compatible process reservation, interruption and observation components from controlled-food-processing-trial where available, recording which code is reused. This is a new moisture-dependent processing effect, not reinvention of those existing operations. Validate lifecycle and conservation in code; established rules must execute without recurrent model approval. Development and review waiting advance no simulation time, grant no inventory and confer no mastery.\",\"learning\":4,\"experienceReview\":\"No pleasure, satisfaction or other reward for requesting, review, registration, learning, starting a batch, elapsed waiting, naming a product or obtaining a preserved label. Setup alone is not verified information gain. An inspection may use existing evidence-deduplicated observation feedback only when a real accessible measurement or visible change supplies personally new, verified information, including informative failure; internal water or decay values must not become free knowledge. Any additional experience hook must be separately implemented with real event evidence, personal applicability, explicit amount/cap, decay and cooldown, and functional deduplication against the existing observation system. Until such a bounded hook exists, this operation awards none. Do not modify protected reward accounts, budget, goals or permissions. Retained nutrition follows the food's actual nutrients and is not reduced by mood; no physical-comfort increase is granted.\",\"visualReview\":\"Emit reusable structured events for setup work, interruption, actual food placement, observed drying or wetting, spoilage, inspection, retrieval, cancellation and material release. Include eventId, tick, actor when applicable, processId, food/support references, actual location, visible quantity and phase, with observation/evidence references where appropriate. Reuse existing item and process renderers and record that reuse. Show real food on its real support only after placement; visible shrinkage or texture changes must follow simulated material changes and be limited to observable properties. A pending or failed setup cannot display dried food, completion effects or preservation success. Completion cues require an achieved configured drying endpoint, not an elapsed timer, and do not certify safety or permanent preservation. Unattended ongoing processes remain visible when observable; hidden moisture, safety or environmental state is not disclosed by visual metadata.\"}]}"}
